messages:
emma-support: FYI — Acme raised an urgent escalation. After the canary swap to rwd-llama-4b-v2 their downstream billing pipeline started charging ~3x. They say structured JSON output is missing the top-level billing tag we rely on ("billingCode") so every chunk gets billed as a separate line item. Paste of their observed response and our logs below.

acme-payload (from customer):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: application/json
transfer-encoding: chunked

{"id":"resp_01","responses":[{"text":"...","tokens":45}],"streaming":true}
{"id":"resp_01","responses":[{"text":"...more","tokens":30}],"streaming":true}
```

Expected single JSON with top-level `billingCode` and `items` array. They show two separate JSON chunks with no `billingCode`, parser falls back to legacy billing path. Reported at 2024-06-20T09:07:36Z.

raj-eng: Can you attach the original request (headers + body) and the model header used? Also did they set `structured_output=true` or use `streaming=chunked` explicitly?

emma-support: Copied from customer: `X-Model: rwd-llama-4b-v2`, body includes `structured_output: true, max_tokens: 512`. They are using streaming=true and expecting a single top-level object emitted and then streaming `data:` chunks that are valid partials for the same object.

marta-ml: Quick hypothesis — model manifest for v2 toggled `emit_separate_chunks: true` to optimize latency, which makes the runtime flush JSON objects per chunk instead of maintaining a single wrapper. That explains separate top-level objects and missing `billingCode` which was injected at wrapper time in our older runtime behavior.

lina-oncall: This is causing customer outage (billing). We should either revert canary immediate or apply a mitigation in the parser/billing pipeline to tolerate chunked outputs. Which is faster?

raj-eng: Fastest mitigation is parser-side: treat multiple top-level JSON objects from a single stream as fragments belonging to same response if `id` matches, and synthesize `billingCode:null` if missing so billing pipeline uses fallback rate (not per-chunk). I'll draft a small shim we can layer in gateway.

marta-ml: Longer-term we should not change chunk emission semantics in a minor model bump. For now revert canary for affected customers. I can also add a model manifest flag check so runtime doesn't override wrapper injection.

lina-oncall: I'll start rollback. @deploy-bot schedule rollback for rwd-llama-4b-v2 -> rwd-llama-4b-v1 for the support tenancy and open dedicated ticket for broader canary pause.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback job created: id deploy_20240620_0912, target rwd-llama-4b-v1, scope: canary-group-2. ETA ~3m.

raj-eng: While rollback runs, @emma-support please ask Acme for a minimal repro curl so we can validate parser shim locally. Example repro: 
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -H "X-Model: rwd-llama-4b-v2" \n  -d '{"prompt":"{...}", "structured_output": true, "stream": true}' \n  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?stream=true
```

emma-support: Sent repro to customer and they confirmed they can reproduce with that curl. They included server log showing `split-chunking: true` in the request trace.

marta-ml: I'll patch model manifest to ensure `emit_separate_chunks:false` for now and add a regression test verifying top-level wrapper & `billingCode` insertion.

raj-eng: I pushed a temporary parser shim to gateway (hotfix branch) that coalesces chunked top-level objects into a single logical response for billing only. Will monitor for false merges.

lina-oncall: Canary rollback finished (deploy_20240620_0912 completed). Please confirm customer billing normalizes after next run.

emma-support: Noted. CS notified Acme and asked them to re-run repro test in ~10m. I'll keep this thread updated. Marking high — followups: patch manifest (marta), gateway shim monitoring (raj), postmortem doc (emma).

deploy-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-20240620-42 (schema/streaming-change caused billing misattribution).

emma-support: Closing loop here once Acme confirms billing returned to normal. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
